item.title: Artists React to the ICE Killing of Renee Nicole Good
item.description: Online and on the streets, protesters are expressing their rage and grief through art.

item.title: Art Against ICE
item.description: How protestors are memorializing Renee Nicole Good, an homage to NYC’s MetroCard, an exclusive look at Joiri Minaya's artist film, and our weekly community columns.

item.title: There’s More to Look at Than Learn in 100 Nights of Hero
item.description: The film faithfully translates the feminist commentary of Isabel Greenberg's graphic novel while deemphasizing its more complex narrative techniques.

item.title: “Sandcastles” Tells the Tale of Two Singapores
item.description: The new short from documentary filmmaker and multimedia journalist Carin Leong explores the transient nature of humankind’s existence through sand.

item.title: The Women Who Were More Than Just Picasso’s Loves
item.description: Sue Roe explores the agency and victories her subjects experienced as women who, we are repeatedly reminded, ardently loved Picasso.

item.title: Uncovering the Secrets of Henri Rousseau’s Paintings
item.description: A new exhibition freshly contextualizes many artworks in the light of his personal story, while conservators conducted revelatory technical studies.

item.title: Beer With a Painter: Michael Berryhill
item.description: “You can’t think your way through a painting,” the artist said during our conversation at his home studio in the Catskills. “You can only act, mark, or feel your way through.”

item.title: Trump Withdraws From Major Culture Preservation Groups
item.description: Two entities focused on global heritage and arts policy are among dozens the White House deemed “contrary to the interests” of the United States.

item.title: South Africa Axes Venice Biennale Proposal Centering Gaza Victims
item.description: Right-wing culture minister Gayton McKenzie reportedly called the subject of artist Gabrielle Goliath’s performance “highly divisive in nature.”

item.title: Here’s Why the LA Art Show Is Worth Your While
item.description: A debut Latin American Pavilion, a video art display, and a mini-retrospective of biennials underscore this fair’s cultural and political relevance.
